result.topic_en: A list of integral formulas (55–61) for logarithms and functions of the elliptic modulus k, k', K, expressed as series in the nome q, followed by a Latin statement of an Abel-type limit theorem for power series on the boundary of the unit circle.
result.transcription:
2.

55) $\int_0 (\log k - \log 4\sqrt{q})\frac{dq}{q} = -4\sum \frac{\psi p}{p^2}\left(q^p - \frac{3q^{2p}}{4} - \frac{3}{16}q^{4p} - \frac{3}{64}q^{8p} - \frac{3}{256}q^{16p} - \dots\right)$
56) $\int_0 -\log k' \frac{dq}{q} = 8\sum\frac{\psi p}{p^2} q^p$
57) $\int_0 \log\frac{2K}{\pi}\frac{dq}{q} = 4\sum\frac{\psi p}{p^2}\left(q^p - \frac{1}{2}q^{2p} - \frac{1}{4}q^{4p} - \frac{1}{8}q^{8p} - \frac{1}{16}q^{16p} - \dots\right)$
58) $\int_0 \left(\frac{2K}{\pi}-1\right)\frac{dq}{q} = 4\sum\frac{\psi(n)\, q^{2^l(4m-1)^2 n}}{2^l(4m-1)^2 n}$
59) $\int_0 \left(\frac{2kK}{\pi}\right)\frac{dq}{q} = 8\sum\frac{\psi(n)\, q^{\frac{(4m-1)^2 n}{2}}}{(4m-1)^2 n}$
60) $\int_0 \left(\frac{2k'K}{\pi}-1\right)\frac{dq}{q} = -4\sum\frac{\psi(n)\, q^{(4m-1)^2 n}}{(4m-1)^2 n} + 4\sum\frac{\psi(n)\, q^{2^{l+1}(4m-1)^2 n}}{2^{l+1}(4m-1)^2 n}$
61) $\int_0 \left(\frac{2\sqrt{k'}K}{\pi}-1\right)\frac{dq}{q} = -4\sum\frac{\psi(n)\, q^{2(4m-1)^2 n}}{2(4m-1)^2 n} + 4\sum\frac{\psi(n)\, q^{2^{l+2}(4m-1)^2 n}}{2^{l+2}(4m-1)^2 n}$

items.english: Before a more accurate investigation of the proposed functions we place the following general theorem as a lemma.

items.english: If the series a0 + a1 + a2, summed in the order written, has a convergent sum, then the function of r expressed by the series a0 + a1 r + a2 r^2 ... converges to the same value as r converges to the limit 1.

items.english: From this it is easily deduced: if a function f(q) of the complex quantity q is represented for moduli of q less than one by the series a0 + a1 q + a2 q^2 ..., then this series, for a value q0 of modulus one, if it has a sum, expresses the value which f(q) attains as q converges to q0 in such a way that only the modulus changes.
